- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.23) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 2–5% relative to model output.
- If model shows sharp upward spike (≥ 10% above recent mean) followed by forecast, cap the overshoot at 5–8% above immediate prior peak to avoid overcorrection.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.16) and model is rising, reduce forecast by 1–3% per negative sentiment unit to counteract pessimism bias.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days) — apply +1.5% to forecast for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated positive spikes (e.g., 3+ consecutive +0.23), model tends to lag — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–5 days to capture momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is > 1.5σ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per sentiment unit below 0.23.
